Finnick likes cooking reels, clothing posts, rugby posts and anything meme related. Finnick skips past political posts, diving compilations, celebrity drama and pet posts.

Use while loops to program an algorithm that decides what type of content will show up in Finnick’s feed again based on his likes and dislikes. The program should print out all eight examples of content with either “keep in feed” or “hide from feed” e.g.

rugby posts: keep in feed

political posts: hide from feed

Task 2: Create a subroutine to randomly select one of the words from the array.

Task 3: Create a subroutine to reverse the selected word.

(Hint: For string reversal, explore a concept called "slicing")

Intermediate 2 by Elena

Finnick wants to find the inspiration from the most successful food instagram account. To do this, he wants to find the best ratio between the number of posts and the number of followers out of a few instagram accounts.

First, extract data from instagram using the Instagramy Module. Here is a resource that teaches you how to install and use this module:

https://www.javatpoint.com/python-instagramy-module

Secondly, extract the number of posts and followers from the following instagram accounts:

buzzfeedtasty

milktpapi

doobydobap

Thirdly, use the formula:

ratio = number of followers / number of posts

The instagram account with the largest value as its ratio is the most successful food instagram account.

Finally, output all three ratios from the given instagram accounts and what the ratio of the most successful instagram account is.

The Instagramy module only works on Jupyter Notebook (google search it to use it)

(Even though this is an intermediate question, I decided to introduce the concept of modules as it is what takes you from intermediate to advanced. If you are struggling with modules, that's ok! You can skip this question and move on)

Use these arrays to do the following:

asks the user for an input as to which post he wants to view

every time the user views the element, increment the number of views by 1

Advanced 2 by Aaleyah

A social media star named Finnick wants to examine his Instagram account to determine which photos have received the most likes and comments. He wants to learn which postings receive the most likes, comments, and interactions. He keeps track of the likes and comments received on his Instagram postings. To read this data and determine the interaction for each article, he wants to create a Python programme.

He wants to apply the algorithm below to determine engagement:

Engagement is calculated as (likes + comments) / the number of followers.

To see which posts are performing the best, he also wants to display the posts in descending order of interaction.

Task:

Write a Python program that can read in the list of Instagram posts, calculate the engagement for each post using the formula provided, and display the posts in descending order of engagement.

Your program should have the following functionalities:

Read the list of Instagram posts from a CSV file:

https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1fHIrVG8q9YDPMmga0XcidVsmZ8FiBXsGpDS7qM2zrSM/edit?usp=sharing

The CSV file will have two columns: "likes" and "comments". Each row will correspond to one post.

Store the number of followers in a variable called num_followers.

Calculate the engagement for each post using the formula provided and store it in an engagement list.

Display the posts in descending order of engagement and the number of likes, comments, and engagement.

Sofea is a TikTok user. Topics she likes include gym, cooking, travel, gardening and art. Imagine her TikTok feed is a 1D array that starts with 5 elements and can constantly be updated. Make a text-based user interface where a subject she likes will be displayed as a string (simulating a post) with equal chance of being about gym, cooking, travel, gardening or art, Provide functions that allow her to like, scroll past, or refresh when given a new post. Make sure user input is validated.

If she likes the post, append a new element to the 1D array with a 5% increased chance of it being that topic (e.g. if she likes ‘easy cake recipe’, the future post should have an increased chance of it being about cooking), make sure the new probability of that topic is stored. Then, clear the console (not the 1D array) and print the next post.

If she scrolls past the post, append a new element to the 1D array with a 5% decreased chance of being that topic, make sure the new probability of that topic is stored. Then, clear the console and print the next post.

Charlotte has a Netflix account with thousands of movies and TV shows. She wants to create a program that can recommend a movie or TV show for her to watch based on her previous viewing history.

Your task is to write a program that uses this data to recommend a movie or TV show for Charlotte to watch. Your program should satisfy the following requirements:

1. The program should read in the "viewing_history.txt" file and store the data in a list of tuples, where each tuple contains the title of a movie or TV show and its genre.

2. The program should read in the "favorite_genres.txt" file and store the data in a list of strings.

3. The program should define a subroutine that takes the list of tuples and the list of favorite genres as input, and returns a list of movies or TV shows that match one of the favorite genres.

4. The program should use the "random" module to randomly select a movie or TV show from the list returned by the subroutine.

5. The program should print the title of the selected movie or TV show to the console.

Advanced 2 by Yu Shen

Valerie is a Shopee user. She really likes buying tech-related stuff. Recently she has been looking to buy a Xiaomi 13, but is not sure which seller to buy from. Using the below dictionary, write a program for Valerie that tallies and displays the total cost of buying a Xiaomi 13 from each seller (including delivery fees and available discounts) then sorts them from least expensive to most expensive, telling her which ones she can afford. She starts with a random amount of money in her account between RM3000 and RM5000.

Valerie must then be able to select which seller she wants to visit and is given the option to buy the product or exit the seller’s page. Visiting a seller’s page clears the previous list from the screen.

If ‘buy’ is chosen, the program must check whether she has enough money in her account. If she does, she’ll be asked for her pin number (the pin number must be 6 digits long and must be a specific permutation of integers). Getting the pin number right will allow her to proceed with the purchase, while getting the pin number wrong more than twice in a row will suspend her account for 365 days.
